 In November 2026, certain recipients of Social Security benefits are to be paid their monthly money slightly earlier than usual.

Update: Oct 25th, 2026 09:52 EDT 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google An upcoming U.S. federal holiday means some Social Security beneficiaries are to receive their November money slightly ahead of schedule . 
 Who’s getting Social Security early?
 On Tuesday, November 10, next month’s Social Security benefits are to be issued a day early to millions of recipients born from the first to the 10th of any month . 
 These beneficiaries usually get their payments on the second Wednesday in the month, but their November distribution date has been brought forward as Wednesday 11 is Veterans Day , a holiday that pays tribute to members of the U.S.’s armed forces.
 A scheme for over 70 million Americans
 Tuesday, November 10 is one of four payment dates on next month’s schedule for Social Security , a scheme with 71.6 million beneficiaries across the U.S. 
 Each month, the program chiefly pays benefits to retired and disabled workers , and to surviving relatives of deceased Social Security-insured workers. Recipients tend to be paid on the second, third or fourth Wednesday in each month, depending on their date of birth . 
 Two groups of people are issued their benefits outside of this birthday-dependent cycle . On the third of the month, Social Security is paid to recipients who: first filed for benefits before May 1997; or combine the program with the Supplemental Security Income scheme.
 In full - November’s Social Security schedule:
 Tuesday, Nov. 3: Dual/long-term beneficiaries 
 Tuesday, Nov. 10: Beneficiaries born 1st-10th 
 Wednesday, Nov. 18: Beneficiaries born 11th-20th 
 Wednesday, Nov. 25: Beneficiaries born 21st-31st 
 How much are monthly Social Security benefits?
 Retirement: $2,034.54 
 Disability: $1,499.41 
 Survivor: $1,636.31 
 Average benefit as of September 2026, per figures published by the Social Security Administration (SSA).
 Social Security set for COLA increase
 Starting with payments issued for January 2027, Social Security beneficiaries are to get a 3.6% rise in their monthly benefit amounts, as part of the SSA’s latest annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA). 
 Across all Social Security recipients, this translates into a hike of about $70 on the current average benefits , which is $1,943.15 per month. For retired workers, who account for over three-quarters of all Social Security beneficiaries, a 3.6% increase means an average pay rise of around $75 per month.
